properties.natural_language: Any contract calling the ECADD precompile at address 0x6 MUST have its input validated for field element range (< p) before point addition is computed.
Any contract calling the ECMUL precompile at address 0x7 MUST have the input point validated against the alt_bn128 curve equation Y^2 = X^3 + 3 before scalar multiplication proceeds.
The zkSNARK verifier contract MUST ensure total gas cost of ECADD (500 each) and ECMUL (40,000 each) operations fits within the block gas limit before initiating verification.
The point at infinity MUST only be represented as (0,0); any other encoding that mathematically equals infinity but uses different byte representation SHALL fail the curve equation check.
When a precompile call fails (invalid point or field element), the call MUST return success=0 with empty return data and all provided gas MUST be consumed.
Surplus bytes beyond the expected input length (128 for ECADD, 96 for ECMUL) MUST be silently truncated without causing validation failure.
All Ethereum client implementations of alt_bn128 curve arithmetic MUST produce identical results for the same inputs to prevent consensus failures.
No valid input to ECADD or ECMUL SHALL cause computation time to exceed what the gas cost (500 / 40,000) accounts for on any supported hardware.
The gas costs of 500 for ECADD and 40,000 for ECMUL MUST accurately reflect worst-case computational complexity across all supported hardware platforms.
The discrete logarithm problem on the alt_bn128 curve MUST remain computationally infeasible for all known attack methods.
After ACTION-CHARGE-ECADD-GAS succeeds, exactly 500 gas MUST have been deducted and input parsing MUST proceed.
After ACTION-CHARGE-ECADD-GAS fails (gas < 500), the precompile MUST transition to STATE-GAS-INSUFFICIENT and then to STATE-ECADD-FAILED.
After ACTION-PARSE-ECADD-INPUT completes, two points (x1,y1) and (x2,y2) MUST be available as parsed state, with short inputs zero-padded to 128 bytes.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-POINTS-ON-CURVE succeeds, the resulting state MUST guarantee Y^2 = X^3 + 3 mod p holds for both input points.
After ACTION-COMPUTE-POINT-ADDITION completes, the result MUST be a valid point on alt_bn128 or the point at infinity encoded as (0,0).
After ACTION-ZERO-PAD-INPUT completes, the input MUST be exactly the expected length with trailing zeros appended.
After ACTION-CHECK-FIELD-MODULUS determines value >= p, the state MUST transition to STATE-FIELD-ELEMENT-OVERFLOW and the precompile MUST fail.
After ACTION-CHARGE-ECMUL-GAS succeeds, exactly 40,000 gas MUST have been deducted and ECMUL input parsing MUST proceed.
After ACTION-COMPUTE-SCALAR-MUL completes, the result s*P MUST be a valid point on alt_bn128 or the point at infinity.
For any valid input to ECADD or ECMUL, the output MUST always be a point on the alt_bn128 curve or the point at infinity (0,0).
EVM bytecode containing JUMP/JUMPI instructions MUST have valid_jump_destinations pre-computed from JUMPDEST markers before execution begins.
When InvalidJumpDestError is raised, all remaining gas MUST be consumed following standard EVM exceptional halt behavior.
The valid_jump_destinations set MUST be pre-computed during contract deployment by scanning bytecode for JUMPDEST (0x5B) opcodes, excluding those within PUSH data.
The valid_jump_destinations set MUST remain immutable throughout the entire execution of a contract call context.
Stack values popped for jump destinations MUST be treated as unsigned 256-bit integers representing bytecode offsets.
Gas costs GAS_BASE, GAS_MID, GAS_HIGH, and GAS_JUMPDEST MUST be consistent across all EVM implementations for a given fork.
After ACTION-POP-JUMP-DESTINATION for a JUMP instruction, validation of the destination against valid_jump_destinations MUST occur before the PC is updated.
After ACTION-EVALUATE-JUMP-CONDITION determines condition == 0, the program counter MUST increment by 1 for sequential execution without attempting the jump.
After ACTION-SET-PC-TO-DESTINATION completes, evm.pc MUST equal the validated destination address exactly.
After ACTION-EXECUTE-STOP executes, evm.running MUST be set to False and no further instructions SHALL be executed.
After ACTION-CHARGE-GAS-MID succeeds for JUMP opcode, the gas counter MUST reflect the GAS_MID deduction and execution MUST proceed.
The EVM program counter MUST always point to a valid bytecode offset: either the next instruction (sequential) or a validated JUMPDEST location.

When KECCAK256 is called with size=0, the operation MUST be valid and return the Keccak-256 hash of empty input (the known constant 0xc5d2460186f7233c927e7db2dcc703c0e500b653ca82273b7bfad8045d85a470).
Memory expansion gas cost MUST grow quadratically to provide natural DoS protection against very large size values for KECCAK256.
The Keccak-256 implementation MUST be cryptographically secure and collision-resistant; no two distinct inputs SHALL produce the same 32-byte hash.
The memory expansion gas cost MUST be sufficient to prevent memory exhaustion denial-of-service attacks from unbounded KECCAK256 input sizes.
After ACTION-POP-MEMORY-PARAMS completes, both memory offset and size values MUST be available as unsigned 256-bit integers.
After ACTION-COMPUTE-KECCAK256 completes, the result MUST be exactly 32 bytes and MUST be deterministic for the same input bytes.
After ACTION-PUSH-HASH-TO-STACK completes, the EVM stack MUST contain the 32-byte hash as a U256 value at the top position.
After ACTION-CALCULATE-WORD-COUNT completes, the word count MUST equal ceiling(size / 32).
After ACTION-SUM-TOTAL-GAS completes, the total gas cost MUST equal GAS_KECCAK256 + (word_count * GAS_KECCAK256_WORD) + memory_expansion_cost.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-STACK-DEPTH fails (stack underflow), execution MUST halt with a stack underflow error.
Block headers received from network peers MUST have their difficulty independently calculated and compared before acceptance; the stated difficulty MUST NOT be trusted.
Blocks submitted by block producers MUST have their stated difficulty verified against the expected difficulty computed using parent block data and fork-adjusted block number.
Parent block difficulty and timestamp data used for difficulty calculation MUST be retrieved from the validated local chain state, not from untrusted peer claims.
The Muir Glacier fork activation block number MUST be a well-defined constant in client configuration (mainnet: block 9,200,000).
The bomb delay offset of 9,000,000 blocks MUST be distinguished from the effective delay of approximately 4,000,000 blocks from the prior activation point.
All Ethereum client implementations MUST compute identical difficulty values for the same block number, parent difficulty, and parent timestamp.
The Muir Glacier fork MUST be deployed and activated before the difficulty bomb causes block times to exceed acceptable thresholds.
Miners and validators MUST upgrade to Muir Glacier-compatible clients before the fork block to avoid producing blocks with incorrect difficulty.
Attackers MUST NOT be able to manipulate the difficulty calculation to produce lower-difficulty blocks after the Muir Glacier fork.
A subsequent hard fork MUST be deployed before the delayed difficulty bomb reactivates (approximately 611 days after Muir Glacier).
After ACTION-COMPUTE-FAKE-BLOCK-NUMBER completes, the fake block number MUST equal max(0, block.number - 9,000,000).
After ACTION-COMPARE-DIFFICULTY determines a mismatch, the block MUST be rejected as invalid.
After ACTION-APPLY-MUIR-GLACIER-DELAY completes, block times MUST return to the target ~13 second interval.
For any block at or after the Muir Glacier fork, the difficulty calculation MUST use max(0, block.number - 9,000,000) instead of the actual block number.
Token transfers from user transactions to the free-for-all bucket contract MUST be validated for token type (ERC-20, ERC-721, ERC-1155), amount, and token ID before being accepted as consideration.
The block proposer's execute() withdrawal call MUST validate recipient, calldata, gas limit, and value parameters before extracting tokens from the free-for-all bucket.
The block proposer's preloadExecutions() call MUST be validated to ensure only the current block proposer can configure preloaded responses.
The free-for-all bucket contract address MUST be a pre-determined constant known to all participants before the system is used.
Consideration value MUST be determined by the block proposer's local business logic and MAY include ERC-20, ERC-721, ERC-1155 tokens or native Ether.
Users MUST order transaction nonces sequentially and handle partial execution scenarios where only some transactions succeed.
This specification MUST be treated as a draft with incomplete security analysis; production deployment MUST NOT proceed without comprehensive security review.
The block proposer MUST honestly execute the evaluation framework without manipulating the execution context to steal consideration or front-run user transactions.
Services communicating with block proposers MUST be available and willing to relay no-ether transactions for the system to be usable.
Attackers MUST NOT be able to predict exact gas costs in a way that enables griefing attacks where proposers lose money on unprofitable evaluations.
The free-for-all contract MUST correctly implement its specified interface and MUST NOT allow tokens to be drained by unauthorized parties.
After ACTION-PROPOSER-CREATE-ETHER-SEND completes, the user account MUST have sufficient Ether to cover gas for all user transactions in the batch.
After ACTION-VERIFY-CONSIDERATION-MATCH completes, the consideration from the second run MUST exactly match the consideration from the first run; otherwise the evaluation MUST abort.
After ACTION-APPLY-BUSINESS-LOGIC determines unfavorable economics, the entire transaction batch MUST be rolled back and rejected without any state changes.
After ACTION-ROLLBACK-REEXECUTE completes, all state changes from the first simulation MUST be fully reverted before the second execution begins.
After ACTION-COMMIT-TO-CHAIN completes, the complete transaction batch including funding, user transactions, and extraction MUST be atomically included in the block.
All wallet_sendCalls requests from DApps MUST be validated for schema, version, chain ID format, call structure, and capabilities before processing.
All wallet_sendCalls requests MUST require explicit user approval before any calls are executed on-chain.
Capability queries from DApps MUST first verify the application is authorized for the requested address before returning any capability information.
For untrusted callers, wallet capability responses MUST be filtered to remove capabilities that could enable fingerprinting of the wallet type.
When atomicRequired=false, the wallet MUST NOT guarantee atomicity; calls MAY be sent in separate transactions, reordered, or partially executed.
Batch identifiers MUST be generated using cryptographically secure random number generation to ensure unpredictability.
Wallets MUST return error 5730 (Unknown bundle id) when wallet_getCallsStatus is called with an ID from a different application than the one that created the batch.
Wallets SHOULD retain batch status for at least 24 hours; applications MUST gracefully handle unknown ID errors near the retention boundary.
Applications MUST correctly report their identity; malicious apps MUST NOT be able to impersonate trusted apps to bypass security checks or access other apps' batch status.
Attackers MUST NOT be able to predict or brute-force batch identifiers within the 24-hour retention window to access other users' transaction status.
The blockchain MUST confirm transactions within a reasonable time so batch status eventually transitions from pending (100) to a final state.
Users MUST understand the difference between atomic and non-atomic execution when approving batched call requests.
Wallet implementations MUST enforce call ordering exactly as specified in the request to prevent security issues in dependent operations.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-REQUEST-SCHEMA succeeds, the request MUST have valid version, chain ID format, and well-formed call objects.
After ACTION-CHECK-DUPLICATE-ID detects a duplicate, error 5720 MUST be returned immediately without further processing.
After ACTION-CHECK-CHAIN-SUPPORT fails, error 5710 MUST be returned indicating the chain is unsupported.
After ACTION-CHECK-ATOMICITY fails when atomicRequired=true, error 5760 MUST be returned.
After ACTION-EVALUATE-RESULTS determines all calls reverted, batch status MUST transition to 500 (Complete Chain Failure).
After ACTION-EVALUATE-RESULTS determines all calls succeeded, batch status MUST transition to 200 (Confirmed).
After ACTION-GENERATE-BATCH-ID completes, the returned ID MUST be unique across all batches for this sender and application.
After ACTION-CHECK-ATOMIC-SUPPORT returns 'ready', the wallet MUST prompt the user for an atomicity upgrade before proceeding.
Batch status MUST be monotonically progressing: once a batch reaches a final state (200, 400, 500, 600), it MUST NOT transition to any other state.
Application-provided IDs MUST be unique per sender per application and MUST NOT exceed 4096 bytes.
Block headers received from network peers for Muir Glacier difficulty validation MUST be independently verified by computing expected difficulty using local parent block data.
Block number data from block producers MUST be validated against the local chain before being used for difficulty bomb delay calculations.
The bomb delay offset MUST be 9,000,000 blocks as specified in EIP-2384; the constant MUST be hardcoded in client implementations.
Muir Glacier mainnet activation MUST occur at block 9,200,000; this value MUST be configured correctly in all client implementations.
The difficulty bomb MUST serve as a forcing function for protocol upgrades; its presence is an intentional design decision.
All clients MUST implement the same difficulty adjustment algorithm to prevent consensus failures and chain splits.
Parent block timestamps MUST be reasonably accurate (within 900 seconds) to ensure correct difficulty calculations.
After ACTION-APPLY-BOMB-DELAY completes, the fake block number MUST equal max(0, actual_block_number - 9,000,000).
After ACTION-CALCULATE-BOMB-COMPONENT completes, the result MUST equal 2^((fake_block_number // 100000) - 2).
After ACTION-COMPARE-DIFFICULTY determines a match, the block MUST be accepted as having valid difficulty.
After ACTION-EXECUTE-BLOCK-TRANSACTIONS completes, all transactions MUST have been processed sequentially and all state changes applied.
After ACTION-COMPUTE-STATE-ROOT completes, the Merkle Patricia trie root MUST deterministically represent the final post-block world state.
Blocks received from P2P peer nodes MUST be validated against the appropriate ruleset (pre-Byzantium or Byzantium) based on block number comparison to the fork threshold.
Block header and body data from peers MUST be validated against both structural and fork-specific rules before acceptance.
Nodes MUST reject blocks that do not follow the appropriate ruleset for their block number; blocks from non-upgraded peers using the wrong ruleset MUST be rejected.
All 9 Byzantium EIPs (100, 140, 196, 197, 198, 211, 214, 649, 658) MUST activate atomically at the fork block with no ordering dependencies.
All network participants MUST upgrade their nodes before the fork block number to maintain consensus on the canonical chain.
Block numbers MUST be monotonically increasing and MUST NOT be manipulable by miners to avoid or re-enable fork activation.
The Ethereum community MUST reach social consensus on the fork block number and included EIPs before activation to prevent contentious forks.
After ACTION-CHECK-BLOCK-NUMBER determines block.number >= 4,370,000 (mainnet), the Byzantium ruleset MUST be applied for validation.
After ACTION-APPLY-BYZANTIUM-RULES succeeds, the block MUST be considered validated under the complete Byzantium ruleset including all 9 component EIPs.
After ACTION-LOAD-CHAIN-CONFIG completes, the node MUST have the correct Byzantium activation block number for its network stored and ready for validation.
For any given block number, exactly one ruleset (pre-Byzantium or Byzantium) MUST apply; the transition MUST be deterministic based solely on block number.
Security Considerations adequacy MUST be determined by EIP editor discretion and AllCoreDevs discussion; criteria MUST include threat modeling, attack vectors, and mitigations.
Rough consensus MUST mean no sustained objections from core developers after AllCoreDevs discussion, not unanimous agreement.
Both the original EIP author and EIP editors MUST be able to initiate resurrection of a stagnant EIP via PR submission.
EIP Editors MUST make impartial decisions about EIP validity based on format and process, not on their personal judgment of proposal merit.
The Ethereum Magicians forum and AllCoreDevs calls MUST remain functional venues for EIP discussion and consensus building.
External links in EIPs anchored to specific commits MUST NOT be modifiable after the commit is published; force-pushed commits MUST be detectable.
Attackers MUST NOT be able to impersonate EIP editors or gain unauthorized write access to the EIP repository to merge malicious proposals.
After ACTION-SUBMIT-DRAFT is merged by an editor, the EIP MUST have status Draft and a unique assigned EIP number.
After ACTION-FINALIZE completes (deadline passed without normative changes), the EIP MUST transition to Final status and only errata/clarifications SHALL be allowed.
After ACTION-WITHDRAW completes, the EIP MUST be permanently in Withdrawn status with a withdrawal-reason field set; the EIP MUST NOT be resurrected.
After ACTION-AUTO-STAGNATE triggers (6 months inactivity), the EIP MUST transition to Stagnant status from whatever active status it was in.
After Last Call period expires with normative changes needed, the EIP MUST return to Review status for further revision.
After ACTION-VALIDATE-PREAMBLE through ACTION-VALIDATE-COPYRIGHT all pass, the EIP MUST be eligible for number assignment.
An EIP in Final or Withdrawn status MUST NOT transition to any other status; these are terminal states.
An EIP MUST NOT progress to Final status without an adequate Security Considerations section.
Clients encountering an empty account in post-merge state MUST treat it as a critical error condition since the behavior is undefined and the state is invalid.
The phrase 'specification is undefined' for empty accounts post-merge MUST be interpreted as a condition that should never occur in a valid network; any occurrence indicates a bug or attack.
Empty account clearing on mainnet MUST have been accomplished via Spurious Dragon cleanup and subsequent state pruning before the merge transition.
The claim that all empty accounts on Ethereum Mainnet were cleared prior to the merge MUST be accurate and verifiable against the state at the merge transition block.
The Spurious Dragon fork's state clearing mechanism MUST correctly prevent creation of new empty accounts in all transaction execution paths.
All test cases and tooling MUST be updated to not include post-merge empty accounts to prevent masking bugs in client implementations.
Attackers MUST NOT be able to craft transactions that leave accounts in an empty state (zero code, zero nonce, zero balance) post-merge.
After ACTION-CHECK-ACCOUNT-PROPERTIES determines an account has code, nonce > 0, or balance > 0, it MUST be classified as not empty.
After ACTION-CHECK-MERGE-BLOCK-HASH matches the mainnet hash, the network MUST be classified as guaranteed to have no empty accounts.
After ACTION-CLEAR-EMPTY-ACCOUNTS completes, the state trie MUST contain zero accounts where code is empty AND nonce is zero AND balance is zero.
In any valid post-merge Ethereum state, no account entry SHALL exist where code is empty AND nonce equals zero AND balance equals zero.
For networks with Spurious Dragon active from genesis AND no empty genesis accounts, the no-empty-accounts invariant MUST hold from block 0.
